A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same role-play-at-scale study. All 20 pages of v2 and 23 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison. The shortened title and added analyses do not obscure the correspondence.

before.justification: V2 reports original MFQ-30 and PVQ-RR experiments, comparisons across persona sets, response distributions, and parser validation results, including extensive appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds inertia and steerability measurements, demographic-effect analyses, and an ordering robustness experiment.

M1.justification: Section 2.1 changes the stated persona-generation rule from approximate population-proportional sampling to uniform per-category sampling. This is a limited revision to the method specification; prompting, parsing and MRAT scoring remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use MFQ-30, PVQ-RR and the same demographic attribute coverage. The added analyses stratify responses or vary questionnaire presentation within these retained tasks; they do not introduce another dataset, population or application domain.

E2.justification: The no-persona baseline and Appendix C's five candidate parsers are retained. No additional competing prompting method is evaluated. Command-R+, already present in parser validation, newly participates as a subject in the pooled demographic analysis.

E3.justification: V3 adds inertia, JSD and Top-2 evaluation metrics, baseline/persona rank comparisons, an MFQ ordering experiment with 60 personas, and a three-model demographic analysis using 50 personas per question. It also revises the stated sampling distribution. These substantially expand the evaluation design, without establishing that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained seed-consistency and sample-size analyses, v3 adds baseline/persona ordering comparisons addressing forced-choice concerns, per-attribute analyses of selective permeability, and randomized-order robustness testing (Sections 3.1, 3.3 and 3.6; Appendix K). These address substantial additional questions about the observed inertia.

E5.justification: V3 adds p-values below 0.001 to the retained correlation results in Table 4, reports a standard-deviation bound of 0.03 for the new inertia estimates in Table 9, and introduces maximum pairwise Cohen's d estimates. The original three seeds remain unchanged; no increase in their number is established.

E6.justification: The existing MRAT scores and correlation coefficients are retained, but substantial results are added. These include dimension/model inertia and JSD values, baseline/persona Spearman correlations of 0.90–0.98, original-versus-randomized ordering scores, and demographic effects such as religion–Tradition d=1.419 and Tradition means ranging from 2.48 to 4.32 (Tables 3, 5 and 9–12). These are additional findings rather than same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 newly defines the normalized-entropy Inertia Index, I(d)=1−H(p_d)/log2(6), states its range, and defines steerability through JSD between baseline and persona response distributions. V2 lacks these formal definitions. No substantial derivation, theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claim of persistent moral/value orientations under persona prompting remains. V3 narrows the contribution framing: its introduction explicitly presents role-play-at-scale as scaling existing persona-injection techniques, and its conclusion drops v2's 'novel method' claim. It also defines the empirical target as behavioral stability.

C2.justification: The new Discussion distinguishes desirable safety-related inertia from problematic cultural under-representation and specifies when demographic sensitivity is appropriate. V3 also discusses stereotype reproduction, short versus richer persona conditioning, parser bias, and the limits of single-turn evaluation. These substantially extend v2's interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: V3 newly states that persona sets, code and analyses are released, while deferring the code link to the camera-ready version; the referenced Appendix A still contains only templates. Actual resource availability is therefore unverified. Existing API identifiers, access dates, default settings and parser details are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds a focused discussion of Russo, Kim, Liu and Long (2025), relating its findings to pluralistic judgments, targeted personas, Socratic debate and structured reasoning. It removes Panickssery (2024) and Shrivastava (2025) and modestly narrows methodological novelty. Most earlier positioning remains.

P1.justification: Most main-text paragraphs are rewritten and compressed, the title is shortened, and the narrative gains dedicated analysis subsections and a Discussion section. Acknowledgments, an AI-use disclosure and Appendices J–K are added. This is extensive editorial restructuring, although Appendices A–I remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Six new analytical tables substantially expand the presentation. V2's illustrative belief table is removed while its underlying findings remain elsewhere, and the correlation table gains p-value columns. Existing figures are largely retained; Figure 3 is resized/downsampled, and Figure 8's incorrect heatmap caption is corrected.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful quantitative definitions, demographic evidence and more specific limitations to v2's largely descriptive account. However, new validation claims have unresolved inconsistencies: Table 5's five score pairs yield Pearson r≈0.49 rather than the stated 0.77, with the correlation's aggregation unexplained; Table 10 also contradicts the claimed universal steerability ordering, for example Sonnet's Fairness JSD exceeds its Ingroup JSD. These problems affect the new supporting evidence, so the net quality direction is uncertain.
